surfaces.name: Qwen Code Desktop (Tauri 2 shell around the Web Shell)
Web Shell served by qwen serve (experimental, browser and phone browser)
VS Code extension (beta), Zed extension and JetBrains integration
Chat channels (Telegram, DingTalk, WeChat, WeCom, Feishu, QQ, email, GitHub, GitLab)
Daemon HTTP+SSE API, SDKs (TypeScript, Python, Java), ACP, managed-agent-server

claims.answer: Terminal CLI, Tauri desktop app (macOS arm64/x64, Linux x64/arm64 AppImage/deb/rpm, Windows x64 installer), experimental browser Web Shell (also phone browser over LAN/HTTPS), VS Code extension (beta), Zed and JetBrains integrations, chat channels and SDKs; no native iOS/Android app.

evidence.title: Bounded source search of the pinned release
evidence.locator: Paths packages/core, packages/cli, packages/web-shell, packages/channels, docs/users; terms: issue tracker, kanban, backlog, rbac, saml, sso, organization role, co-prompt, presence, review queue, deploy
evidence.finding: No persistent issue tracker, role model, SSO, presence or review queue was found in the inspected paths; Agent Board is a file-based local task board and tenant IDs in the managed server are header-asserted.

evidence.title: Agent Board task store
evidence.locator: BoardTaskStatus (line 36); createBoardTask (lines 108-120, owner optional, status pending); claimBoardTask (lines 203-216, rejects when in_progress and owned by another actor)
evidence.finding: Board tasks are persisted records with an optional owner label and status pending, in_progress or completed; claimBoardTask sets owner and in_progress and throws when another actor already holds an in_progress task; actor names are labels validated by name only, not authenticated. Documentation adds qwen board done with a note, ask/answer/decline, and storage under ~/.qwen/boards until pruned.

evidence.title: qwen-live coding agent detector
evidence.locator: agent-detector.ts lines 44-80 (qodercli, qwen, gemini, claude, codex entries with ACP args); adaptor/acp-adaptor.ts line 769 spawn of the agent command; packages/qwen-live/README.md setup wizard
evidence.finding: The qwen-live package (standalone Live voice daemon, also reachable from an experimental Web Shell setting) scans PATH for qodercli, qwen, gemini, claude and codex and its ACP adaptor spawns the chosen agent as a child process over JSON-RPC stdio to run coding sessions; non-native agents use adapter packages.

evidence.title: Qwen Code v0.28.4 usage statistics logger and settings schema
evidence.locator: qwen-logger.ts USAGE_STATS_HOSTNAME (line ~83) and getUsageStatisticsEnabled() gate (line ~219); packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled (label 'Enable Usage Statistics', category Privacy, default true, showInDialog true)
evidence.finding: At v0.28.4 QwenLogger sends RUM usage events to an Alibaba Cloud RUM endpoint (gb4w8c3ygj-default-sea.rum.aliyuncs.com) whenever usage statistics are enabled. privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled defaults to true and is shown in the interactive /settings dialog as 'Enable Usage Statistics' under Privacy; it can also be set in settings.json.

changes.author: agent:ADE-84
changes.summary: Independent review: the Agent Board documentation (v0.27.4) shows qwen board claim, done --note, --owner, task states pending/in_progress and settled records persisted under ~/.qwen/boards, so PLAN-06, PLAN-07 and COORD-02 understated board operations; the issue-tracking 'no' mapping contradicts those findings and is rejected.

before.answer: Agents can read and write the experimental Agent Board through qwen board commands with an actor label; records are local files, not a shared issue system.

after.answer: Agents and humans share the experimental Agent Board through qwen board commands: create a task, claim it (sets owner and in_progress; a different actor cannot then claim it), mark it done with a note, ask and answer questions, with a --as actor label recorded; records are local files for one OS user, not a shared authenticated issue system.

changes.author: agent:ADE-84
changes.summary: Independent review: the Agent Board documentation (v0.27.4) shows qwen board claim, done --note, --owner, task states pending/in_progress and settled records persisted under ~/.qwen/boards, so PLAN-06, PLAN-07 and COORD-02 understated board operations; the issue-tracking 'no' mapping contradicts those findings and is rejected.

before.answer: No native issue management; sessions are archivable and an experimental local Agent Board holds simple tasks.

after.answer: No native issue management beyond an experimental local Agent Board of simple tasks with owner label, pending/in_progress/completed state and notes; sessions are archivable.

changes.author: agent:ADE-84
changes.summary: Independent review: the Agent Board documentation (v0.27.4) shows qwen board claim, done --note, --owner, task states pending/in_progress and settled records persisted under ~/.qwen/boards, so PLAN-06, PLAN-07 and COORD-02 understated board operations; the issue-tracking 'no' mapping contradicts those findings and is rejected.

before.answer: No assignment or claims between humans; Agent Board owners are recorded labels; cross-session protocol buffers messages; no exclusive ownership.

after.answer: Agent Team leaders assign workstreams to teammates; the experimental Agent Board offers claims where an in_progress task cannot be claimed by another actor label, cross-session messages queue, and nothing authenticates the actor or starts the owner.

changes.author: agent:ADE-84
changes.summary: Independent review: the monorepo's experimental qwen-live package detects installed Qoder CLI, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, Claude Code and Codex and drives them over ACP, so ACC-02 'only the Qwen Code harness runs in the product' was too strong and the nine agents 'no' mappings are removed.

before.answer: Embeds the Qwen Code agent harness and speaks OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen API protocols with local providers; exposes itself over ACP to other tools; a delegation skill lets other agents drive Qwen Code; does not host other coding CLIs as harnesses.

after.answer: Embeds the Qwen Code agent harness and speaks OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen API protocols with local providers; exposes itself over ACP to other tools; a delegation skill lets other agents drive Qwen Code; the experimental qwen-live package in the same monorepo can drive installed Qoder CLI, Gemini CLI, Claude Code and Codex over ACP (Claude and Codex through adapter packages) alongside Qwen Code.
